name: New Retail Store Opening Proposal
description: A warm editorial retail proposal for connecting trade-area evidence, brand positioning, space planning, launch operations, and store economics in one opening-day narrative.
style_guide:
# New Retail Store Opening Proposal

## Design intent

Create a decision-ready opening proposal for a design-conscious neighborhood retail concept. The deck should connect local demand, positioning, merchandise, spatial experience, campaign operations, launch readiness, investment, and store economics. Its character is warm, urban, and considered rather than glossy: ivory paper, charcoal type, burnt-orange editorial emphasis, forest-green operational signals, orthographic planning diagrams, and one strong architectural photograph on the cover.

The reference previews are visual-language examples only. Rebuild all store names, addresses, catchments, customer segments, merchandise mixes, opening dates, budgets, sales forecasts, staffing numbers, and financial assumptions from the current workspace. Do not reuse the sample retailer, neighborhood, venue, or metrics.

## Canvas and grid

- Use a fixed `1280 × 720 px` 16:9 canvas with `58–66 px` side margins, a `30–38 px` upper project frame, and a `24–30 px` source footer.
- Use a 12-column grid with `18–22 px` gutters. Align headlines, map bounds, merchandise bands, experience steps, campaign milestones, and financial exhibits.
- Reserve `110–145 px` for section label, conclusion-style headline, and a brief implication. Let one diagram, map, or operating exhibit dominate the lower field.
- Prefer balanced `6/6` cover splits, `7/5` map-and-metrics layouts, two-panel positioning pages, and full-width timeline structures.
- Keep `22–28 px` between major modules and `10–16 px` within cards. Use negative space and fine rules rather than decorative containers.
- Body pages remain warm ivory. Use charcoal panels only for a decisive brand proposition, key operating readout, or financial summary.

## Color system

### Core palette

- Warm retail ivory: `#F5F1E8`. Use for the main canvas and planning-diagram ground.
- Paper white: `#FFFDFC`. Use for inset maps, charts, tables, and cards.
- Charcoal ink: `#20201F`. Use for primary typography, diagrams, and high-authority financial panels.
- Burnt orange: `#D8531D`. Use for key phrases, catchment rings, active milestones, launch dates, and commercial emphasis.
- Forest green: `#3E654B`. Use for residential or lifestyle context, operational readiness, steady-state performance, and secondary series.
- Sand beige: `#DED3BA`. Use for merchandising zones, quiet surfaces, timelines, and spatial plans.
- Warm gray: `#8D887F`. Use for metadata, inactive states, map context, and source notes.

### Semantic use

- Orange means customer attention, opening urgency, or a commercial decision; it should not mark every heading.
- Green means established neighborhood value, readiness, or a verified healthy operating state.
- Charcoal panels signal a firm proposition or financial conclusion, not generic decoration.
- Use red only for a genuine blocker or financial risk and pair it with a label and owner.

## Typography

- Use `Inter`, `Aptos`, `Helvetica Neue`, or another modern retail sans-serif.
- Use the italic cut for one editorial phrase in a headline, such as a positioning idea, journey concept, or launch cadence. Do not use script fonts.
- Cover title: `50–62 px`, regular, with one orange italic phrase. Page headline: `31–39 px`, regular to medium. Section label: `9–11 px`, uppercase, tracked. Body: `14–17 px`. Tables and map labels: `10–13 px`. Sources: `8–10 px`.
- Financial values use tabular numerals. Keep currency, period, basis, and units adjacent to every figure.
- Avoid all-caps headlines and excessive bold. The hierarchy should feel editorial and spatially confident.

## Components

- Cards are rectangular, flat, and lightly ruled. Use white, ivory, sand, charcoal, or green surfaces with no drop shadow and minimal corner radius.
- Metric cards pair a short label with one large value and a one-line definition or source context.
- Use orange section numbers, fine dividers, project name, confidentiality, and page count as a persistent frame.
- Merchandise mix may use a proportional horizontal band with direct percentage labels. Do not use unlabelled decorative color blocks.
- Experience steps use numbered rows with a clear action, spatial location, and operational purpose.
- Tables need comfortable row spacing, short labels, aligned values, and one highlighted decision or total.

## Charts and diagrams

- Favor catchment maps, positioning matrices, merchandise-mix bands, annotated floor plans, customer journey loops, launch timelines, channel plans, staffing or readiness summaries, budget donuts, milestone Gantt charts, and quarterly sales bars.
- Maps must include a defined catchment method, scale or travel-time basis, location markers, and source date. Do not imply precision from a decorative map.
- Spatial diagrams should label entrances, zones, circulation, service points, back-of-house, accessibility, and operational constraints when relevant.
- Timelines should show owners, dependencies, decision gates, and opening-critical paths, not only marketing moments.
- Financial charts must distinguish capex, pre-opening expense, working capital, inventory, revenue, margin, breakeven, and payback assumptions.
- Use orange for the active launch path, green for a stable or ready state, and charcoal for totals. Avoid 3D charts.

## Composition families

### Architectural cover

Split the canvas between an ivory title field and one full-height exterior or interior retail photograph. Use a compact opening-date card over the image and keep project metadata aligned at the bottom.

### Trade-area diagnostic

Use a map or catchment exhibit across two-thirds of the page and a metric grid plus customer-segment strip beside it. State the location conclusion in the headline before showing the evidence.

### Positioning and assortment

Pair a price-versus-design positioning matrix with a charcoal brand proposition and a proportional assortment band. Explain what the positioning excludes as clearly as what it includes.

### Space and customer journey

Use an annotated floor plan or zoning diagram with a directional journey, then add four or fewer experience principles. Connect each spatial decision to dwell time, service, conversion, or operational flow only when supported.

### Opening campaign and operations

Build a full-width countdown with phases, channels, press or creator activity, staffing, inventory, systems, and readiness gates. Make the go/no-go conditions visible.

### Investment and sales plan

Pair launch budget and master schedule with a dark financial panel containing revenue, margin, transaction, breakeven, or payback logic. Keep assumptions and scenario basis next to the numbers.

## Imagery

- Use licensed, location-relevant retail exteriors, interiors, fixtures, material details, wayfinding, merchandise, or neighborhood context.
- Favor warm natural light, honest materials, tactile surfaces, and human-scale urban scenes. Keep the image grade warm but not sepia.
- Body pages should use maps, plans, and evidence rather than lifestyle collages.
- Use one minimal line-icon family for location, commuter, creator, shopper, merchandise, café, staffing, and systems.
- Avoid generic luxury storefronts, crowded shopping bags, handshakes, staged cash registers, and unrelated influencer imagery.

## Content integrity

- Do not invent addresses, population, income, footfall, catchment times, conversion, dwell time, rent, store size, inventory, staffing, impressions, revenue, margin, transactions, breakeven, or payback.
- Separate measured site data, third-party demographic data, comparable-store evidence, operator assumptions, vendor quotations, and forecast outputs.
- State geography, period, source, sample, and method for local demand and customer segmentation.
- Clarify whether merchandise mix refers to floor area, SKU count, inventory cost, units, or expected revenue.
- Financial pages must identify currency, tax treatment, contingency, lease assumptions, capex versus opex, gross or contribution margin, and forecast scenario.
- Opening readiness must have owners, dates, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and a clear escalation path.
- If evidence is missing, omit the claim or label it `assumption`, `target`, `concept`, `forecast`, or `to be confirmed`. Do not manufacture numbers to complete a map or dashboard.

## Avoid

- Do not copy preview store names, location, customer profiles, assortment, floor plan, opening date, budget, forecast, staffing, campaign, or contact details.
- Do not turn the proposal into a generic brand mood board with no operating or financial logic.
- Do not use orange on every label, fill, and chart; preserve it for attention and decision points.
- Do not use glossy gradients, glass cards, heavy shadows, oversized rounded corners, photorealistic 3D floor plans, or retail clip art.
- Do not present a catchment radius as proven demand or a traffic count as conversion.
- Do not hide lease, licensing, accessibility, construction, inventory, staffing, system, or contingency risks.
- Do not show a single financial forecast without its assumptions, scenario, and sensitivity.
